form_fields.label: Why Cancierge?
form_fields.value: You give cancer patients a second opinion in minutes instead of weeks, built with oncologists and heading for MDR Class IIa. I want to build an AI core where every change is measured against what clinicians expect, which is how I already work.

form_fields.value: €80,000 gross/year (posting range €80,000–90,000; profile range €60,000–75,000 is below their band, so quote the bottom of theirs).

questions.q: Walk us through how you'd design an evaluation harness for a model that gives treatment guidance.
questions.a: Fix a labelled ground-truth set with clinical experts, pick metrics per task (precision/recall for extraction, retrieval metrics, answer correctness), version data + configs + seeds so every run is repeatable, compare setups side by side. Evidence: thesis RAGAS + PytrecEval harness against chemist ground truth; Kniit loop against SAP-derived ground truth (33/45 → 93/90 precision/recall).

questions.q: How do you control overfitting and pick learning rates / hyperparameters in PyTorch?
questions.a: Train/validation/test splits (time-based for time series), early stopping, weight decay, dropout, learning-rate schedules, small search over key hyperparameters. Evidence: LSTM at Cognizant (96% test accuracy, held up on unseen data), RF/XGBoost/LSTM comparison at Covestro, QLoRA fine-tuning. Revise PyTorch internals (autograd, optimizers, schedulers, DataLoader) before the CTO round: this is the main gap.

questions.q: How would you turn prototype logic from our Head of AI into production code?
questions.a: Small modules with clear interfaces, typed configs, tests around each step, evaluation in CI so every change is measured. Evidence: sole developer at Kniit reporting to the CTO; domain experts approve changes via Expert Interface.
